subject: Q4 QBR slate: voice alignment + data ownership
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: QBR slate voice & data ownership — initial pass

Hi team,

Kicking off a focused pass on the Q4 QBR slate. High-level asks:
- Decide one "narrative voice" for the executive run (concise, customer outcome-first).
- Assign a single data owner per section (Growth, Ops, Cost, Reliability, Product).
- Surface any outstanding data gaps by EOD Thursday so we can lock visuals.

I've attached a quick inventory of existing datasheets and who last touched them (QBR_data_inventory.xlsx). Please reply with the owner you take (or nominate someone) and any known blockers.

Suggested timeline: internal freeze for slides by Friday 11/05 COB, then internal review with Greg and Hana on Mon 11/08. If this timeline doesn't work for your org, flag now.

Thanks — Jonas

Attachment: QBR_data_inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet stub, 18 rows)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: QBR slate voice & data ownership — initial pass

Thanks Jonas — I'll own the exec summary voice and shepherd the slide narrative. Quick proposals below:

- Voice: "Outcome-first, signal + ask" (two-sentence opener, then 3 supporting bullets).
- Owners: Growth -> Mina Haddad; Ops (SLA/Latency) -> Neha Kapoor; Cost -> Marissa Cole; Product metrics -> Mina (shared); Reliability incidents -> Neha.
- Blockers: Mina noted a gap in week-over-week DAU segmentation; Neha flagged one delayed incident RCA.

I'm attaching an initial one-pager draft for the exec summary (exec_summary_draft_v0.pptx). Please add comments in-slide by Thursday.

Also: recommend we loop Greg (Horizon Capital) into the readout deck on Monday but keep the initial freeze internal. If everyone agrees, I'll prepare a 1-slide appendix with investor-facing notes so we can redact/expand depending on audience.

Jasmine

Attachment: exec_summary_draft_v0.pptx (pptx stub, 2 slides)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: QBR slate voice & data ownership — initial pass

Jasmine — thanks, voice guidance makes sense. A few quick edit requests after scanning exec_summary_draft_v0: 

- Growth slide: swap absolute M/M ARR delta for ARR run rate contribution (shows runway). Mina, can you provide ARR-by-cohort table?
- Ops: use 90-day rolling latency P95 instead of single-week snapshots; Neha, please confirm availability to generate that by Thursday.
- Risks/asks: add a short bullet about model-cost exposure tied to new embeddings ingestion (we should call out mitigation or reserve spend).

I'll inline comments on slide 2. Jonas — do you want me to take point on compiling the risk ask language?

Date: 2026-11-05T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: QBR slate voice & data ownership — initial pass

Adding the ARR-by-cohort export and refreshed OKR numbers. See attached okrs_metrics_2026q4.csv — includes: cohort ARR, MRR deltas, DAU segments, and embedding ingestion volumes.

Notes:
- DAU segmentation: week-over-week segment is available but the 90-day retention curve requires a join we're still validating; ETA for final curve is Mon 11/08 AM.
- ARR run rate table is included in tab 3 of the export.
- Embedding ingestion spike in week 40 is traced to a single customer integration — tracking with CS for attribution.

If you want me to reshape into a small slide graphic, I can draft a compact chart (1 slide) by EOD Friday.

Attachment: okrs_metrics_2026q4.csv (csv stub, 1 file)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Greg Stevens <greg.stevens@horizoncap.com>, Hana Park <hana@lpfirm.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T14:00:00-08:00
Subject: QBR slate — internal freeze & investor readout plan (attached)

Team — thanks for the fast turnaround. We're at the internal freeze stage for the core slides; please consider the attached v1 final as the current authoritative source for internal review.

Key notes:
- Owners confirmed: Growth/Product -> Mina; Ops/Reliability -> Neha; Cost & Risk -> Marissa; Exec voice -> Jasmine.
- Outstanding: final 90-day retention curve (Mina) — targeted Monday 11/08 AM.
- Investor-facing appendix: included as slide 10 in the attached deck so Greg and Hana can see supplemental context without affecting narrative flow.

Next steps:
1) Greg/Hana — I'm adding you both to the investor appendix only for Monday's readout; please treat slides as pre-read.
2) Internal reviewers — please leave any in-slide comments by Monday 11/08 10:00 AM PT.
3) I'll send the DocuSign approval link for the final investor deck after the readout.

Attachments: QBR_slate_v1-final.pptx (pptx stub, 12 slides)
Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/QBR-2026-drafts, https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/HC-9876, https://www.docusign.com/sign/QBR-approval-987

Thanks — Jasmine
